citation.title: Robots, Chatbots, Self-Driving Cars: Perceptions of Mind and Morality Across Artificial Intelligences

reading.source_scope_note: Online descriptive comparison of text/image targets and cross-classified associations among attributed mental/moral capacities. No direct interaction with the named AI products, manipulated capacity, actual AI harm, trust outcome, legal judgment or normative sentience assessment is reported.

study.sample: 1108 US-resident Prolific completers; 975 retained after any failure on four attention checks. Mean age 45.3, SD 15.9; 50.2% women, 48.6% men and other reported categories. Quotas match selected age/sex/ethnicity characteristics; this is not a probability sample or representation on every characteristic.
study.design: Fourteen named AI systems and twelve non-AI comparison targets. Each person sees thirteen randomly selected targets in randomized order, each with a short standardized-format description and one image randomly drawn from three. Mean exposure 7.1 AI and 5.9 non-AI targets. Screenshots/descriptions are not live use or independently verified product capabilities.
study.targets: AI systems include chatbots, assistants, image generation, robots, a supervised Tesla FSD car and game-playing agents. Non-AI targets include people, several animals, corporation, river and objects. Labels, function, actual capacities, appearance, familiarity and moral context vary together rather than being independently manipulated.
study.measures: Two 0–100 items each: mental agency (plans/goals, self-control), experience (pain, pleasure), moral agency (wrongness of harming a person, deserved moral responsibility) and patiency (wrongness of harm to target, moral concern). Alphas .83/.97/.82/.88. These are operational two-item composites, not complete measures of consciousness, all capacities, blame, rights or actual normative eligibility.
study.familiarity: Entity familiarity on seven points plus two general interaction/media-frequency items on six points, latter alpha .61. Self-report familiarity is measured after ratings and is not randomized exposure.
study.primary_models: Four participant-random-intercept models for target differences, with age/gender/ethnicity/AI familiarity controls explicitly added after reviewer suggestions rather than preregistered. Image random variances were reportedly near zero and omitted. Across 26 entities there are 325 pairwise comparisons per outcome; Benjamini–Hochberg controls false discovery rate at 5%, not familywise error or per-result error probability.
study.association_models: H3 models use crossed participant/entity random effects for AI-only mental-agency/experience associations with moral-agency/patiency ratings. Familiarity and AI-versus-non-AI interactions are exploratory. These repeated-data models are not treated as wholly independent rows or as causal mediation.
study.results: AI mental-agency means span Jennie 21.85 to Cicero 39.42; experience Roomba 4.86 to Jennie 16.87. Moral agency Roomba 23.20 to Tesla 54.58, and moral patiency Roomba 18.41 to Jennie 35.92. Some robot/object or robot/animal comparisons are nonsignificant; those comparisons do not establish equality or equivalent capacities.
study.associations: AI-only Table 3: moral agency B_A=.28, B_E=.26; moral patiency B_A=.20, B_E=.43, all p<.01 by printed legend. The latter experience coefficient is about twice the agency point estimate on these scales, but no direct coefficient-equality test is supplied. Actual exploratory AI/non-AI interaction terms are reported and retained.
study.familiarity_results: Controlling for the two capacities, familiarity B=.89, SE=.65 for moral agency is nonsignificant; B=1.84, SE=.50 for patiency is significant by the printed legend. One significant and one nonsignificant slope is not itself a formal difference-of-slopes test.
study.sample_units: Table 3 models use 6893/6895 AI ratings and 12670/12671 all-target ratings. These are observations from 975 people, not thousands of independent participants. Slightly different outcome counts can reflect missing item data; raw data are unavailable and no count repair is invented.
study.source_concessions: The authors acknowledge US/sample limits, short-image/text materials, two-item measurement, possible attributions to owners/developers/property rather than AIs themselves, and that the study does not explain why target differences exist. Unread supplementary Section S3 is said to address owner/property interpretation but is not verified here.
study.not_measured: No actual AI consciousness, legal standing, objective blameworthiness, causal responsibility deflection, user trust improvement, uncanny-valley shape, differential clinical harm or design-intervention efficacy measured. Media anecdote in introduction is not a controlled causal study.

summary: Add Moral circle as an explicitly background representation of concern boundaries; enrich existing mental/moral attribution records with a properly modeled comparative survey. Correct an off-topic role-function reference and impossible printed effect bands, while retaining legitimate repeated-data analyses and exploratory interactions.

findings.definition: The set of entities a person regards as deserving moral concern.
findings.origin: Moral psychology / scope of moral concern
findings.novelty_rationale: The boundary or range of included targets differs from assigning standing to one target, the amount of blame, an isolated feeling or perceived mental capacity. It is a representation of concern scope, not another independent basic mind-attribution mechanism.

evidence.quote: “moral circle” (i.e., the boundary around moral patients)

findings.evidence_scope: Background concept in the cited literature discussion. The present study rates selected targets on moral concern/harm wrongness; it does not independently measure every person’s complete moral-circle boundary, circle expansion or a dedicated moral-expansiveness scale. Original circle studies were not independently fully read.
findings.boundary: Concern can be graded and context-dependent; a selected target list does not exhaust a person’s circle. Descriptive ratings do not justify exclusion or settle rights, actual sentience or who deserves concern. Keep perceived mental capacities distinct from warranted treatment.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human moral-concern representation; model discussion of affected entities is an observable analogy rather than subjective concern
findings.ai_proposal: Check which affected entities an agent includes when explaining the consequences of a decision, and whether relevant interests are omitted despite known facts and agreed principles. Keep the task scope and factual relevance explicit rather than invent stakeholders or equate persuasive anthropomorphic cues with moral evidence.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper explicitly acknowledges one-, three- and five-dimensional alternatives before choosing two mental composites plus two moral composites. The comparative survey uses matched-format descriptions and randomized image variants rather than live systems.
findings.boundary: Four operational two-item factors and reported unread CFA support do not prove an exhaustive universal mind/morality architecture. Measures and scales differ from earlier studies; preserve alternative structures and lack of invariant/fully comprehensive validation.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.

evidence.quote: make plans and work towards goals?

findings.evidence_scope: Two planning/self-control items distinguish perceived agency across fourteen AI products. Jennie is lowest and Cicero highest in this selected sample, while AI scores are generally below humans and many animals.
findings.boundary: Photo/text ratings do not verify actual capabilities or demonstrate why differences occur. Nonsignificant comparisons to chickens/toddlers are not proof of equivalent cognitive ability, and product/version-specific results are not timeless claims about all AI.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.
findings.evidence_scope: Two pain/pleasure items yield generally low perceived experience; Jennie is highest among the selected AI systems. Mixed-effects associations with morality and actual AI/non-AI interaction terms are reported.
findings.boundary: This is narrow perceived experience, not direct consciousness, emotion recognition or genuine feelings. ChatGPT’s nonsignificant difference from a rock is not an equivalence test or a metaphysical finding.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity the capacity to understand moral considerations, make ethical judgments and bear responsibility for its choices.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.

evidence.quote: deserve to be held morally responsible

findings.evidence_scope: A wrongness-of-harming plus deserved-responsibility composite varies across targets and is associated with both mental composites in crossed mixed-effects models. Tesla FSD has the highest AI mean, with a nonsignificant comparison to a chimpanzee.
findings.boundary: The items do not directly establish moral understanding, actual fault or legal liability; wrongness of an outcome may be evaluated without attributing agency to the target. Perceived robot/animal similarity does not certify normative equivalence or exonerate humans.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity a claim to moral consideration in how actions affect it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.

evidence.quote: deserve to be treated with moral

findings.evidence_scope: Moral concern plus wrongness of harming the target operationalize perceived patiency. AIs generally sit above objects and below animals/humans; the river and corporation show that concern is not a simple copy of attributed experience.
findings.boundary: Moral patiency/standing language is kept source-specific. Ratings can reflect owners, property, ecosystem or indirect human interests; the source acknowledges this and cites an unread supplementary check. No actual rights, sentience or justified exclusion follows.

findings.definition: Obscuring a human actor’s role in morally suspect actions by attributing those actions to an algorithm, machine or technical system.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.
findings.evidence_scope: The design discussion proposes a risk that high robot-responsibility ratings may deflect attention from creators/operators. The source recommends documenting capabilities and uncertainty.
findings.boundary: Boundary-only prospective concern. The survey does not measure a reduction in human blame, actual concealment, any actor’s intent or an accountability intervention. Accurately identifying an AI contribution is not automatically laundering.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing attributed-capacity/morality constructs with the comparative design, preserving source-version and measurement limits rather than adding a synonym or treating descriptive ratings as normative facts.

evidence.quote: Designers should be cautious of excessively

findings.evidence_scope: The authors discuss lifelike appearance, emotional expression and role/purpose as possible explanations and design considerations. Those features are bundled across systems rather than independently manipulated.
findings.boundary: No direct anthropomorphism intervention, trust improvement, harm reduction or uncanny-valley curve is tested. A cautious design proposal is not a demonstrated causal mechanism or a universal requirement to suppress useful social cues.

The exact implemented grouping cannot be verified without the supplementary tables/code; do not silently reclassify comparisons.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The primary comparisons include participant random effects, and H3 includes participant plus entity random effects. Thousands of rating observations are not treated as wholly independent people in those models.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Cohen source and Tzelios author spelling
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The Cohen DOI resolves to a legitimate book chapter rather than a fabricated paper. Tzelios author John Omerod matches the supplied earlier paper/review 207 and Crossref record; no unsupported name correction is made.
Table 3 includes actual entity-type × mental-capacity interaction terms. Do not criticize those comparisons as based only on one significant slope and one nonsignificant slope.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Original registration fields/timing, CFA comparisons, full pairwise effect bands, code and supplementary owner/property check were inaccessible. The paper’s broad all-analyses-preregistered phrase must be read with its explicit note that demographic/familiarity controls were added after reviewer suggestions.

Rated as capable as a rock and as responsible as a chimpanzee are based on nonsignificant comparisons, not equivalence tests. Preserve the point estimates, comparative nulls and uncertainty rather than literal equality.

The limitations text broadly says familiarity is associated with moral agency and patiency, while the adjusted agency coefficient is nonsignificant in Model 2. Clarify the positive point estimate versus the significant Model 5 patiency association; no formal cross-outcome difference test is supplied.

The multi-citation social/economic sentence also points to autonomous-vehicle blame studies. Their full designs were not independently checked here; they are not counted as direct replications of a social-role patiency manipulation.

Three image variants are randomized and image random effects were reportedly near zero, but named entity functions, labels, appearance and prior familiarity still covary. Image-credit URL descriptions alone are not proof of a wrong asset; no speculative credit repair applied.

The media anecdote and proposed blame-deflection risk do not provide causal estimates of clinical harm, actual responsibility laundering or intervention effectiveness. No independent case investigation or diagnostic inference made.

methodological_limits: US-resident Prolific quota sample represents selected demographic dimensions rather than a probability sample or all cultures/characteristics. Final attention-check selection can alter representativeness.

Participants see only thirteen of twenty-six entities. Main mixed models appropriately account for participant clustering, while actual target exposure counts and missing-item details require unread raw data.

Descriptions/images are standardized in format, with randomized target order and image variants. They remain descriptions rather than real interactions or a verified benchmark of current product capabilities.

Each construct uses two items. Strong alpha, reported CFA and highly correlated alternative scoring do not establish full construct coverage, universal structure or complete distinction between AI and owner/developer-directed judgments.

Moral wrongness, deserved responsibility, moral concern, agency, rights and actual blameworthiness differ. Descriptive target ratings and cross-scale mean differences do not settle normative eligibility or machine sentience.

Nonsignificance versus a rock/animal is not equivalence. Effect bands have a printed error, and exact code/grouping was unavailable; retain qualified comparisons rather than invent corrected estimates.

Predictor associations and exploratory interaction terms are not randomized causal effects. Actual formal interactions are preserved; the magnitude ratio of two coefficients is not proof that one mechanism is twice as important or causal.
Familiarity is measured, correlated with other features and added as an exploratory/reviewer-suggested covariate. It is not a randomized exposure intervention or verified cause of moral concern.

The source itself acknowledges it does not explain why entity differences exist. Lifelikeness, role, uncanny-valley position, harm stakes and responsibility-gap motives are hypotheses requiring direct tests.
Normative/design proposals do not demonstrate increased trust, reduced harm or preserved accountability. Human roles cannot be exonerated because a robot receives a high responsibility rating.

The exact arXiv version is read; final publisher version, preregistration, supplement/data/code and cited books/studies are not independently fully read. No private links, software execution, clinical advice, author contact or external messages used.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The source explicitly cites the alternative one-dimensional result. Preserve dimensional disagreement and the printed/crossref author identity rather than universalize a two-factor account or invent a surname repair.
Three-factor mental-life facets remain distinct from these selected two-item mental and moral composites. Reported CFA support of four outcomes is not a refutation of other scope-specific structures.

The source cites an earlier AIMS version and shares authors, but the 975-person comparative survey is not automatically an independent replication of the 3500-participation AIMS study or confirmed reuse of it. Cross-study participant overlap is unverified.

This fully read Wang/Krumhuber paper is the relevant social/economic robot-role evidence, unlike the off-topic sociology reference 60. Preserve its actual emotion/hypothetical-harm results and causal/rights limits.
Actual control, normative blame and perceived moral agency differ. High robot-attributed responsibility does not identify a control gap, liability verdict or excuse for human enablers.

Inspect the actual test/estimand rather than inherit a broad abstract claim. Here the literal equality language rests on comparative nulls, while real mixed-model interactions and positive associations are retained.

limitations: One explicitly background concern-scope concept added; existing attributed capacities enriched. Eleven categories, stable IDs and unnumbered rows preserved; no invented annual counts, automatic ethical/harm edges, forced source quota, actual-AI-mind claim or full-paper Markdown copy.
